classification: Static reference-firmware analysis; no recovery/updater executable run. Not a trace from the phone.
method: Extract RECOVERY_RAMDISK as data; parse Android boot v0 page/ramdisk bounds; bounded gzip decompression with CRC and newc entry bounds; copy selected regular files only. Test embedded dload ZIP CRC and read its updater as ELF data. Use LLVM objdump 9.0.3svn, ELF unwind ranges and manually reviewed address/string references for selected functions.

selected_functions.observation: Uses a 32-byte value in updater state and calls the list-validation function; a successful validation marks its completion flag.
Calls the line/hash check; failure takes the version-list error path and returns nonzero. Additional state-dependent paths exist.
Iterates CR/LF-separated lines, hashes candidate strings and compares 32 bytes. An all-0xff comparison value has special handling.
Calls a SHA-256 routine on a line then compares 32 output bytes. SHA-256 identification additionally checked against all eight standard IV words at virtual address 0x23b4d0.
Reads OEMINFO item 156, length 32, through the rmt_oeminfo_read wrapper into the state buffer later passed to base-version validation. A failed read sets a separate error/state flag.
Creates a wait thread and logs a 300-second wait for USB update start.
Checks a start flag between wait calls with argument 1, counts up to 300 and then calls WaitingTimeoutReboot.
Logs no action in 300 seconds and follows a reboot path containing sys.powerctl and reboot, literals; selected range is a bounded excerpt, not a full function audit.

interpretation: A 300-second no-action reboot path is consistent with the owner-observed 5% screen and automatic return. Exact phone recovery byte equality and elapsed time were not measured.
Version checking is supported by inspected conditional control flow, not only string presence. However the actual OEMINFO item 156 value was not read from this phone.
The confirmed Android component properties, package VERSION labels and internal BASE_VER strings are distinct inputs. Do not substitute a getprop value for the stored 32-byte comparison value.
Presence of SHA-256/list validation does not establish signature validity or hardware rollback counters, and does not prove which condition this exact downgrade would encounter.
The embedded wrapper updater-script names an unrelated Qualcomm target; it was not executed or used as a MAR-LX1A flash recipe. The separate compiled DLOAD updater is the analyzed program.

host_preparation_checks.runtime: PowerShell 7.7.0 on Linux; Windows PowerShell 5.1 execution not yet tested
results: Large APP size and SHA-256 passed
Existing valid output verified without overwrite
Failed extracted output retained as .part, not promoted
Unrelated ZIP traversal member not extracted
host_preparation_checks.scope: Offline fixtures and real cached-archive verification; no Windows phone or network transfer test.

limits: Reference .562 archive is not byte-identical to the owner HiSuite base capture by known source size. Current phone recovery byte equality remains unverified.
No version-check modification, OEMINFO change, temporary loader, firmware write, downgrade, persistent unlock or custom boot tested.
